title: Why Your Android Phone Is Slow and What to Fix First
html:
An Android phone usually gets slow for three plain reasons: storage is almost full, too many apps are busy in the background, or one app is misbehaving. Check them in that order, change one thing at a time, and look at your numbers before you move on. Restarting and updating comes first because it costs nothing. A factory reset is the last step, not the first.

Last updated: 10 Oct 2026.

Tested on a vivo V23 Pro (model V2132) running Funtouch OS 14 (Android 14), Android security update January 2025, on 10 Oct 2026.

Before you change anything, write down three numbers

If you do not measure before, you cannot tell whether a fix worked. Note these first:

  • How much storage is free (Settings, then Storage).
  • How long one heavy app takes to open from a cold start. Close it from recent apps, tap it, and time it with a stopwatch.
  • How much battery you lose in a normal hour of use.

Before any cleaning, my vivo V23 Pro's RAM and storage screen showed 113 GB used of 128 GB. By category: System 34 GB, Apps 29 GB, Images 21 GB, Videos 17 GB, Documents and others 4.4 GB, Games 846 MB. RAM showed 7.43 GB used (8 GB + 8 GB total).

1. Restart, then update

Restart the phone first. Then check for updates: open Settings, tap System, then Software updates. Google says to connect to Wi-Fi and charge to at least 75% before you update, because updates can be large.

Samsung phones have a quick tool: Settings, then Device care, then Optimize now. Samsung describes it as clearing unneeded items from memory, deleting unnecessary files, scanning for malware and closing apps running in the background.

Menu names change from brand to brand. If you cannot find an option, type its name into the search box at the top of Settings.

2. Free up storage

Go to Settings, then Storage, then Free up space. Pick a category, tap Select files, and move what you do not need to the Trash. The same screen has a Smart Storage switch that clears backed-up photos and videos automatically. Google Files ("Files by Google") has a Clean tab that suggests junk, duplicates and unused apps.

If you back up photos to Google Photos, you can delete the copies on the phone. Check that the backup finished first.

Clearing an app's cache is done in Settings under Apps. Google notes that the exact menu varies by phone. It removes temporary files only, but the app has to rebuild them, so the app can feel slower for a moment afterwards. Do it for one or two apps that are huge, not for everything.

How full is too full? Neither Google nor Samsung publishes an official percentage, so there is no magic number. Measure it on your own phone.

After a quick cleanup the same screen showed 111 GB used of 128 GB, down from 113 GB, so about 2 GB came back. Apps went from 29 GB to 28 GB. System (34 GB), Images (21 GB) and Videos (17 GB) did not change. I did not time app launches before and after, so I cannot say the phone got faster. The point is how little a quick cleanup frees on a phone this full: the big gains would have to come from photos, videos and apps.

3. Remove apps you do not use

There are three easy ways to find them:

  1. Settings, then Apps, then Unused apps (Android 13 and newer). For apps you have not opened for a long time, Android deletes temporary files, takes back permissions, stops them from running in the background and stops their notifications.
  2. Files by Google, then Clean, then the "Delete unused apps" card. It asks for usage access so it can see which apps you rarely open.
  3. Play Store, then your profile picture, then Manage apps & devices, then Manage. Pick the app and tap Uninstall.

While you are there, look at any app you do not remember installing. If one looks wrong, see our guide on how to check Google Play Protect.

4. Stop apps from working in the background

Open Settings, then Apps, then See all apps. Tap an app, then App battery usage, then Allow background usage. You will see three choices: Optimized, Restricted and Unrestricted. Google explains that with Adaptive Battery on, apps you use less often run less while you are not using them.

One warning from Google: if you turn off battery optimisation for an app, that app can run more while you are not using it, which can use more battery than needed. So leave most apps on Optimized and only switch an app to Restricted if it keeps showing up as a heavy user.

To find the heavy ones, look at Settings, then Battery, then Battery usage. An app you rarely open that sits near the top is the one to look at first.

5. Check RAM expansion (virtual RAM)

Some phones use part of your storage as extra memory. On Samsung it is called RAM Plus, and the setting is under Settings, then Battery and device care, then Memory, then RAM Plus. Samsung says it uses your storage as virtual memory, so you can keep more apps open and launch them faster. Because the extra memory is carved out of your storage, a nearly full phone has less room to give.

Other brands have a similar option under names like Memory extension or Extended RAM. The name and the menu differ by brand. Only the Samsung option is documented in the sources below.

Whether it helps you is something you can test. Pick six apps you really use. Open them in the same order, then switch between them for ten minutes and count how many reload from scratch. Do the same with the option off. Fewer reloads is the benefit. Slower switching is the cost.

On my vivo V23 Pro, About phone shows the RAM as 8 + 8 GB. Tapping the info icon next to it says: "The RAM can be dynamically extended by up to 8 GB. Some storage space will be taken up." I have not tested the phone with this switched on and off, so I cannot say how much it helps.

6. Is it one bad app? Try Safe mode

Safe mode starts the phone with your downloaded apps switched off. Google's advice: use the phone normally and see if the slowness goes away. If it does, an app is likely the cause. Then remove recently installed apps one at a time, restarting normally after each, until the problem stops. How you enter and leave Safe mode differs by phone, so Google points you to the maker's support page.

We have a separate guide with more detail: Android Safe Mode explained.

7. Factory reset: the last step

A factory reset erases all your data from the phone, so only do it when the steps above did not help. Google says you need your Google Account username and password and your screen lock PIN, pattern or password, because you must enter them after the reset. It also recommends charging the phone to at least 70%, and it says the reset can take up to an hour. Back up first to your Google Account. After the reset you have to be connected to sign in to your Google Account.

If you do reset, put the apps back gradually instead of restoring everything at once, and check your three numbers again after each batch. That way you will see which app brings the slowness back. Do not forget your two-factor codes: see our Google account security checklist before you wipe.

Things I would skip

  • "Booster" and cleaner apps. Everything above uses tools already on your phone or from Google, so there is no need to install another app that wants broad permissions.
  • Developer options tweaks. You may see advice to set the animation scales to 0.5x. Android's developer documentation describes these settings as changing how fast animations play. That makes the interface feel quicker, but it does not make apps load faster.

When none of this works

If the phone is still slow after a clean reset, the cause is probably hardware or age: a worn battery, slow or failing storage, or a phone that no longer gets updates. To see where your phone stands, open Settings, then About phone, then Android version, and look at the Android security update date.

If storage still looks full when you have deleted files, read why Android storage stays full after deleting files.

What to do next

  1. Restart and update.
  2. Free up storage and re-check your numbers.
  3. Remove unused apps.
  4. Look at background usage, and change one app at a time.
  5. Test RAM expansion on and off if your phone has it.
  6. Use Safe mode if you suspect one app.
  7. Reset only when everything else has failed, and back up first.
